methodological_rigor.justification: Multicenter observational study with centralized HER2DX testing (Reveal Genomics, analytically validated) and central pathology review for TIL, TLS, TIME, and histologic subtype following International Immuno-Oncology Biomarker Working Group guidelines. 410 prospectively accrued patients from 24 Spanish hospitals with clearly defined eligibility. Statistical methods are appropriate: parametric/non-parametric univariate tests, chi-square/Fisher, Pearson correlation, bivariate logistic regression adjusted for HR status, and multivariable logistic regression for pCR with pre-specified variable selection (P<0.10 in univariable). Weaknesses include local HER2 IHC, no explicit sample-size justification, no multiplicity correction across the many features tested, and lack of multiregion/single-cell data to address heterogeneity (acknowledged).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study directly informs the ongoing effort to de-escalate or intensify therapy in HER2+ early breast cancer by linking HER2DX genomic outputs to established pathologic predictors. The multivariable finding that HER2DX pCR score is the sole independent predictor of pCR (OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.08-2.97, P=0.030) supports its clinical utility. Observational real-world biomarker cohort maps to Oxford LoE 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK applies as this is a prognostic/predictive biomarker study. Reporting includes eligibility, central testing, score definitions with published cut-offs, pathology methods (International TIL Working Group, WHO subtypes), ethics (IRB Hospital Clinic Barcelona, GDPR compliance), and robust statistical description. Gaps against REMARK include lack of explicit pre-specification of primary hypotheses, no sample-size calculation, incomplete description of missing data handling for the 160/410 patients without pCR outcomes, and no REMARK checklist. No repository or code sharing statement; HER2DX is a commercial assay.

novelty_literature.justification: HER2DX has been extensively validated in prior cohorts (ShortHER, SCAN-B, APT, ATEMPT, PerELISA, PHERGain, inflammatory BC, CLEOPATRA, CompassHER2 pCR) and several patient-level meta-analyses. The present work's novelty is a systematic comparison of HER2DX signatures to comprehensive standard pathology including TIL, TLS, and spatial TIME distribution in a large real-world cohort, with concordance/complementarity analyses. This is a meaningful incremental extension confirming biological coherence and complementarity rather than a new discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear, well-organized manuscript with appropriate figures (distribution plots, boxplots, heatmap, scatter plots) and a correlation heatmap linking HER2DX modules to pathology variables. Methods and statistical analyses are well described. Discussion integrates recent trial evidence (ATEMPT, APT, CompassHER2, CLEOPATRA) and acknowledges limitations (local HER2 IHC, no multiregion profiling). Minor issues include dense tables and some redundancy between score-specific sections.

key_strengths: Large prospectively collected real-world HER2+ early breast cancer cohort (n=410) from 24 Spanish centers with centralized HER2DX testing and central pathology review

Systematic comparison of all three HER2DX scores (pCR, risk, ERBB2) against comprehensive pathology (grade, HR, HER2 IHC, Ki67, TIL, TLS, spatial TIME, histology) with biologically coherent associations (IGG-TIL r=0.59, proliferation-Ki67 r=0.50, luminal-pCR score r=-0.83)
Multivariable demonstration that HER2DX pCR score is the only independent predictor of pCR after neoadjuvant trastuzumab-based therapy (OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.08-2.97, P=0.030)
Clinically relevant stratification identifying the 57% 'favorable' HER2DX group and characterizing the ~10-15% ERBB2-low subgroup with central reclassification
key_concerns: Local HER2 IHC determination introduces interlaboratory variability despite central HER2DX testing (acknowledged)

Observational cross-sectional biomarker analysis cannot directly demonstrate treatment-decision impact; 160/410 patients lacked pCR outcomes and selection biases in neoadjuvant allocation could confound analyses
No explicit multiplicity correction across the many univariate comparisons; no power justification
Commercial assay (Reveal Genomics) precludes external reproducibility of the algorithm; no data/code availability beyond institutional procedures
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sound, clinically useful real-world biomarker validation extending prior HER2DX literature by systematically aligning genomic scores with contemporary pathology including TIL/TLS/TIME, appropriate for a strong Tier 2 venue such as Clinical Cancer Research or ESMO Open, not Tier 1 given incremental nature.
